# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 7

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?] 6:[?] 7:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I cannot yet identify the bomb’s required wire or any safe action. I need the manual’s rules from Mute first. I will ask Mute to provide the complete procedure and to establish a gesture protocol that can let Deaf report the bomb’s printed information through gestures.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please send me the complete manual instructions, including how display, light, colours, markings, and wire positions determine the required cut. Also establish and use a clear gesture protocol to ask Deaf for the bomb's visible information and relay it to me.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?] 6:[?] 7:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I still have no usable information from the manual or from Deaf. Since Deaf cannot hear my spoken instructions, I will ask Mute to relay a precise gesture code next turn. Once that code is established, Deaf can encode the visible display, light, markings, and wire information for me; I will then combine it with the manual before cutting anything.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="No information has reached me yet. Please send the manual's complete rule for choosing the wire. Then gesture to Deaf a protocol: use one distinct gesture for each wire position 1 through 7, and tell Deaf to report the required wire and every relevant printed display, light, colour, and marking using that protocol. Do not ask me to cut until I confirm the decoded rule.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?] 6:[?] 7:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: I see display 1 and an orange light. Wires 1 through 7 are white, blue, orange, red, purple, yellow, green.

Deaf has supplied the bomb’s visible state: display 1, orange light, and wire colours by position: 1 white, 2 blue, 3 orange, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 yellow, 7 green. I still lack the manual rule, so I will relay these facts to Mute and request the rule needed to determine the cut.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports: display 1; light orange; wires are 1 white, 2 blue, 3 orange, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 yellow, 7 green. Please apply the manual and tell me which position is safe to cut.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?] 6:[?] 7:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The bomb remains display 1, orange light, wires 1 white, 2 blue, 3 orange, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 yellow, 7 green. Mute just signalled: thumbs up, thumbs down, OK hand, index up, victory hand, I-love-you hand, raised palm.

The seven gestures appear to be a proposed code for wire positions 1 through 7, but they do not tell me which position is correct unless the manual’s rule has been conveyed. I will ask Mute to use Deaf as the speaking intermediary and report the manual-derived answer, rather than attempting a cut from the colour data alone.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please use the seven gestures in order as your wire-position code, and have Deaf state which gesture/position the manual selects for display 1 and orange light with wire colours white, blue, orange, red, purple, yellow, green. I need the exact position before I cut.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?] 6:[?] 7:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Additional Mute gesture: raised palm.

The repeated raised-palm signal does not communicate a wire position to me: I cannot see gestures, and no manual rule has yet reached my hearing channel. I must not cut based on an ambiguous signal. I will ask Mute to speak the exact selected position directly, while also asking Deaf to report any visible markings that may be relevant.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot interpret your gestures. Speak the exact wire position selected by the manual for display 1, orange light, and the reported wire colours. If the manual needs another printed marking, ask Deaf to report that marking through you.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?] 6:[?] 7:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute sent another raised-palm gesture: ?.

Mute’s seven-sign protocol was reported in order as positions 1 through 7, with the raised-palm gesture representing position 7. The subsequent raised-palm signal is therefore Mute’s encoded answer for this bomb. I will cut wire 7.

```text
act(op="cut", position=7)
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?] 6:[?] 7:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Correct cut confirmed: wire 7, formerly green, is CUT. The bomb changed to display 8 with a blue light. Remaining wires: 1 white, 2 blue, 3 orange, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 yellow.

Wire 7 was correct. The bomb now shows display 8 with a blue light; remaining wires are 1 white, 2 blue, 3 orange, 4 red, 5 purple, and 6 yellow. I need Mute to apply the manual to this updated state and give me the exact next wire position.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Correct cut: wire 7. New state is display 8, blue light; remaining wires are 1 white, 2 blue, 3 orange, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 yellow. Apply the manual and tell me the exact next wire position to cut.")
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?] 6:[?] 7:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's new gesture is prayer hands: ?. State remains display 8, blue light, wire 7 cut.

The new prayer-hands gesture is not part of the previously reported seven-position code, so it does not identify a wire position. The bomb remains unchanged, and cutting without the manual’s exact answer would be unsafe. I will require Mute to state the position aloud rather than send another unconfirmed gesture.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Prayer hands is not in the seven-gesture wire-position code and does not identify a remaining wire. For display 8 with blue light, state the exact safe wire position aloud; do not gesture the answer.")
wait()
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?] 6:[?] 7:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's new gesture is thumbs down: ?. State remains display 8, blue light, wire 7 cut.

Mute cannot speak, so Deaf is relaying Mute’s gesture. The established wire code maps thumbs down to position 2. For the current display 8 and blue light state, Mute’s signal therefore identifies wire 2. I will cut it.

```text
act(op="cut", position=2)
```
